72882-the-face-of-china.title: The Face Of China
72882-the-face-of-china.creator: Unknown
72882-the-face-of-china.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. My first voyage to China was unspeakably distasteful, and as we neared Hong Kong we were suddenly caught up in the tail of a typhoon and carried for forty-eight hours wherever it pleased to take us. Most of that time we were without food, and could not even get a cup of tea; while we found it hard work to cling to a seat.

arxiv-2103-09028.title: Rogue waves on the background of periodic standing waves in the derivative NLS equation
arxiv-2103-09028.creator: Jinbing Chen, Dmitry E Pelinovsky
arxiv-2103-09028.description: Abstract The derivative nonlinear Schrödinger (DNLS) equation is the canonical model for dynamics of nonlinear waves in plasma physics and optics. We study exact solutions describing rogue waves on the background of periodic standing waves in the DNLS equation. We show that the space-time localization of a rogue wave is only possible if the periodic standing wave is modulationally unstable.

arxiv-2112-06016.title: Accurate approximations of density functional theory for large systems with applications to defects in crystalline solids
arxiv-2112-06016.creator: Kaushik Bhattacharya, Vikram Gavini, Michael Ortiz, Mauricio Ponga, Phanish Suryanarayana
arxiv-2112-06016.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kaushik Bhattacharya, Vikram Gavini, Michael Ortiz, Mauricio Ponga, Phanish Suryanarayana. This chapter presents controlled approximations of Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT) that enable very large scale simulations. The work is motivated by the study of defects in crystalline solids, though the ideas can be used in other applications. The key idea is to formulate DFT as a minimization problem over the density operator, and to cast spatial and spectral discretization as systematically convergent approximations.

arxiv-2210-13231.title: Analysing Training-Data Leakage from Gradients through Linear Systems and Gradient Matching
arxiv-2210-13231.creator: Cangxiong Chen, Neill D. F. Campbell
arxiv-2210-13231.description: Abstract Recent works have demonstrated that it is possible to reconstruct training images and their labels from gradients of an image-classification model when its architecture is known. Unfortunately, there is still an incomplete theoretical understanding of the efficacy and failure of these gradient-leakage attacks.

arxiv-2301-00005.title: Intrinsic Motivation in Dynamical Control Systems
arxiv-2301-00005.creator: Stas Tiomkin, Ilya Nemenman, Daniel Polani, Naftali Tishby
arxiv-2301-00005.description: Abstract Biological systems often choose actions without an explicit reward signal, a phenomenon known as intrinsic motivation. The computational principles underlying this behavior remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigate an information-theoretic approach to intrinsic motivation, based on maximizing an agent’s empowerment (the mutual information between its past actions and future states).

arxiv-2406-15216.title: A Highly Granular Temporary Migration Dataset Derived From Mobile Phone Data in Senegal
arxiv-2406-15216.creator: Paul Blanchard, Stefania Rubrichi
arxiv-2406-15216.description: Abstract Understanding temporary migration is crucial for addressing various socio-economic and environmental challenges in developing countries. However, traditional surveys often fail to capture such movements effectively, leading to a scarcity of reliable data, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. This article introduces a detailed and open-access dataset that leverages mobile phone data to capture temporary migration in Senegal with unprecedented spatio-temporal detail.

arxiv-2411-13171.title: Parameterized Geometric Graph Modification with Disk Scaling
arxiv-2411-13171.creator: Fedor V. Fomin, Petr A. Golovach, Tanmay Inamdar, Saket Saurabh, Meirav Zehavi
arxiv-2411-13171.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fedor V. Fomin, Petr A. Golovach, Tanmay Inamdar, Saket Saurabh, Meirav Zehavi. The parameterized analysis of graph modification problems represents the most extensively studied area within Parameterized Complexity. Given a graph G G and an integer k ∈ ℕ k\in\mathbb{N} as input, the goal is to determine whether we can perform at most k k operations on G G to transform it into a graph belonging to a specified graph class ℱ \mathcal{F} .

arxiv-2508-21810.title: QR-LoRA: QR-Based Low-Rank Adaptation for Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
arxiv-2508-21810.creator: Jessica E. Liang, Anirudh Bharadwaj
arxiv-2508-21810.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jessica E. Liang, Anirudh Bharadwaj. The growing scale of Large Language Models (LLMs) has necessitated the development of parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as a promising approach, reducing the number of trainable parameters by applying low-rank updates to pretrained weights. While standard LoRA learns both update factors directly, several recent variants first initialize those matrices via an SVD of the pretrained weights—an operation that can be expensive on large models and yields singular vectors that are not always easy to interpret.

arxiv-2512-18837.title: Generative Modeling through Spectral Analysis of Koopman Operator
arxiv-2512-18837.creator: Yuanchao Xu, Fengyi Li, Masahiro Fujisawa, Youssef Marzouk, Isao Ishikawa
arxiv-2512-18837.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuanchao Xu, Fengyi Li, Masahiro Fujisawa, Youssef Marzouk, Isao Ishikawa. We propose Koopman Spectral Wasserstein Gradient Descent (KSWGD), a generative modeling framework that combines operator-theoretic spectral analysis with optimal transport. The novel insight is that the spectral structure required for accelerated Wasserstein gradient descent can be directly estimated from trajectory data via Koopman operator approximation which can eliminate the need for explicit knowledge of the target potential or neural network training.

pmc-10507852.creator: Nousheen Akber Pradhan, Amir Ali Barket Ali Samnani, Kiran Abbas, Narjis Rizvi

The available evidences does not provide comprehensive insight into primary health care (PHC) system functioning across low- and middle- income countries (LMICs) during the pandemic.

pmc-11381835.title: Integrating cardiovascular risk assessment into mobile low-dose CT lung screenings in rural Appalachia: A comprehensive analysis of the relationship between lung cancer risk, coronary artery calcium burden, and cardiovascular risk reduction strategies
pmc-11381835.creator: Seher Berzingi, Kara Piechowski, Emily Hendricks, Mark Colantonio, Asuwin Anandarm, Gregory Perkowski, Tyler Miller, Justin Conte, Sameh Nassar, Belal Kaseer, Marcelino Mederos Liriano, Juan Carlo Avalon, Kyle Chapman, Brijesh Patel
pmc-11381835.description: ObjectiveMobile low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) lung screenings are part of an outreach program in rural Appalachia to detect early lung cancer. Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring on LDCT can identify calcium deposits in coronary arteries and can prompt consideration of risk modification for prevention of cardiovascular disease (CVD) events.

pmc-11420853.title: Nanomedicines in diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancers: an updated review
pmc-11420853.creator: Jiajia Wang, Xuan Zhang, Jiazhen Xing, Lijian Gao, Hua Lu
pmc-11420853.description: Prostate cancer (PC) is the third most common male cancer in the world, which occurs due to various mutations leading to the loss of chromatin structure. There are multiple treatments for this type of cancer, of which chemotherapy is one of the most important.

pmc-11432487.title: Risk Factors of Velamentous Cord Insertion in Singleton Pregnancies—A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11432487.creator: Antonios Siargkas, Ioannis Tsakiridis, Athanasios Gatsis, Catalina De Paco Matallana, Maria Mar Gil, Petya Chaveeva, Themistoklis Dagklis, Michal Kovo
pmc-11432487.description: Objective: This meta-analysis aims to quantitatively summarize current data on various potential risk factors of velamentous cord insertion (VCI). A better understanding of these risk factors could enhance prenatal identification both in settings with routine screening and in those where universal screening for cord insertion anomalies is not yet recommended.

pmc-11648798.title: Blunt trauma-induced complete esophageal avulsion: A case report on surgical intervention and clinical insights
pmc-11648798.creator: Nathaniel Grabill, Mena Louis, Nicole Redenius, Mariah Cawthon, Brian Gibson
pmc-11648798.description: Blunt esophageal injury is an exceptionally rare condition, with complete esophageal avulsion being almost unprecedented in adults. This case study details the clinical presentation, surgical management, and postoperative course of a 50-year-old male who sustained a complete esophageal avulsion following blunt abdominal trauma.

pmc-12403488.title: RHBDF2 governs microglial neuroinflammation during cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury and is positively regulated by the m6A reader YTHDF1
pmc-12403488.creator: Lisi Xu, Ruonan Zhang, Xiaolin Zhang, Bing Liu, Xiuli Shang, Daifa Huang
pmc-12403488.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundNeuroinflammation mediated by microglia activation is the key pathological mechanisms for cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury (CIRI). This study investigated the role and underlying molecular mechanism of Rhomboid 5 homolog 2 (RHBDF2) in neuroinflammation during CIRI.MethodsThe in vivo middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion (MCAO/R) mouse model and in vitro HMC3 microglia subjected to oxygen glucose deprivation and reperfusion (OGD/R) were established to mimic CIRI.

pmc-12676154.title: Radiation Dose Optimization in a Multicenter CCTA Program
pmc-12676154.creator: Rachel Roedding, Juan Gaztanaga, Shant Manoushagian, Danielle Opela, Juan C Lopez-Mattei, Richard A Chazal
pmc-12676154.description: BackgroundExcessive radiation exposure from coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) increases lifetime malignancy risk. Internal review within a 5-hospital health system revealed median system-wide doses above best-practice targets, with high intercampus variability.Project RationaleDose optimization is a modifiable patient safety measure supported by national guidelines, with evidence that reduction can be achieved without loss of diagnostic quality.

pmc-13033608.title: A multidimensional analysis of neuropsychiatric lupus: clinical, biological and imaging insights from systematic evidence
pmc-13033608.creator: Karim Matmat, Hélène Jamann, Amin Maazouzi, Kévin Bigaut, Michel Maitre, Jérôme De Seze, Ayikoé-Guy Mensah-Nyagan, Hélène Jeltsch-David
pmc-13033608.description: ObjectiveNeuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus (NPSLE) is among the most challenging manifestations of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), affecting the central and peripheral nervous systems with diverse symptoms. Despite its prevalence, the diagnosis and management of NPSLE remain complex due to the heterogeneity of clinical presentations and the lack of specific biomarkers.

pmc-13346102.title: Inside the Minds of Professional and Elite Athletes: A Qualitative Exploration of Perspectives on Cannabinoid Use in Contact Sports
pmc-13346102.creator: Elizabeth S Thompson, Jane Alcorn, Robert B Laprairie, Noelle Rohatinsky, Payam Dehghani, J Patrick Neary
pmc-13346102.description: Background:As cannabis legalization expands and professional sports organizations reassess cannabinoid policies, elite contact sport athletes are increasingly exposed to cannabis use for therapeutic, recovery, and recreational purposes. Despite these shifts, limited evidence-based education and persistent stigma may hinder informed decision-making and athlete-clinician communication.

pmc-13450085.title: Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis and Preliminary Peripheral Blood Evaluation Identify ASAP2 as an Exploratory Candidate Molecule Associated with Complete Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome
pmc-13450085.creator: Cheng Luo, Chengzheng Duan, Shiyu Xu, Jiali Xu, Shengxin Wang, Lulu Zheng, Xianmei Yu, Dongjuan He
pmc-13450085.description: BackgroundComplete androgen insensitivity syndrome (CAIS) is a rare 46,XY disorder/difference of sex development (DSD) caused by impaired androgen receptor (AR) function. Although AR sequencing is central to diagnosis, downstream transcriptional consequences of AR dysfunction and accessible readouts of androgen-pathway disruption remain unclear.

pmc-13505602.title: Reflection- and Curriculum-Based Instruction Tuning for Diabetes-Specialized Large Language Models: Model Development and Evaluation Study
pmc-13505602.creator: Jaesung Hwang, Deniise Liz Namayanja, Donghyeon Park, Hongfang Liu
pmc-13505602.description: BackgroundEffective diabetes management requires continuous interpretation of glycemic trends, personalized dietary guidance, and sustained patient education. Although large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for health-related applications, existing general-purpose and biomedical models often struggle with diabetes-specific reasoning and instruction-following, limiting their reliability for domain-focused tasks such as clinical question answering and dietary recommendation tasks.

pmc-13673264.title: Early parathyroid hormone elevation after denosumab therapy following parathyroidectomy: a diagnostic pitfall
pmc-13673264.creator: Hiroyuki Yamashita, Hisakazu Shindo, Daisuke Tatsushima, Yusuke Mori, Kento Katsuyama, Shinya Sato
pmc-13673264.description: Persistently elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) after parathyroidectomy is often attributed to residual disease but may reflect altered calcium (Ca) homeostasis. The impact of denosumab on perioperative PTH interpretation remains unclear. A 77-year-old woman presented with a hypercalcemic crisis and was initially managed at another hospital.
